text:
The Bruins are 15-7-1 and on pace for about 100 points, and the first thing to understand is how. Their chances are only a little better than their opponents' (51% of the expected goals, which measure the quality of chances), but they have allowed about 10 fewer goals than those chances predict. Our numbers say the record is running roughly five points ahead of the play. Michael DiPietro has helped lately, with a .926 and 3.5 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

The best thing on the roster is a defense pair. Hampus Lindholm and Charlie McAvoy have taken 65% of the expected goals together at 5-on-5 and outscored teams 14-7. Up front, Elias Lindholm has 11 points in 10 games and scored a hat trick against Washington on Saturday; 98.5's Ty Anderson notes he is paced for 32 goals and 71 points. His line with Casey Mittelstadt and rookie James Hagens has outscored opponents 8-3.

The off-ice story is Pavel Zacha. Several outlets have linked him to trade talk, including a Yahoo piece tying him to a Dylan Larkin deal, and an insider suggested an extension looks unlikely. He centers the top line with David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka (9-5 at 5-on-5), so any move would ripple.

Our playoff odds put Boston at 83%. What we'd watch: whether the 5-on-5 play catches up to the goaltending before the goaltending cools.
